title: Apocalypsis cum figuris
subtitle: On the never-ending relentless march through time, the future will come again.

trails.title: Distortion
trails.description: ​​The ITU Radio Regulations won't be released for a few more years, so just use what you have.

content.text:
"Team 'Difference Engine,' this is HQ. Southeast district sweep complete, and Arcana's presence has not been detected. Abort mission, link up with Team 'Tungsten Wire,' and proceed to ... Hello? Team 'Difference Engine,' come in! Damn these primitive comms! If I'd been born in this era, I'd have chosen any career without radios."
"Got anything on your end?"
"The Field Squad's got cut off, but my device kept picking up crosstalk. There's this Royal Mail Ship reporting a sudden submarine attack, requesting Entente warship assistance. So I guess it's 1917."
"Can't be 1917. Multiple bands are broadcasting about Hollweg. More likely 1915, if you ask me."
"No way it's 1915! My liaison team mentioned the Battle of Verdun has been over for ages. Optimistically, we might be at war's end with everyone analyzing the aftermath!"
"Can't be optimistic. From what I'm hearing, Austria-Hungary is still holding strong, and the Ottomans are no slouches. Probably Manus Vindictae has had a hand in this."
"Yeah, maybe the arcanists in this war—Wait, Team 'Difference Engine'! This is HQ. Go ahead!"
The Foundation's communication officer grabs a pen, nearly splashing ink on the other one's face.
The scratch of pen on paper lasts a full minute before stopping.
"What did he say?"
"Two years ago, the Compiègne negotiations failed. It's 1920."

items.text: Apocalypsis cum figuris
Antarctic Plain

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: This is ...
Moldir steps down from the helicopter, watching drops float upward.

items.speaker: Buddy Fairchild
items.text: Butter my backside and call me a biscuit! Rain pullin' itself right off the ground and risin' up into the sky! I ain't never seen nuttin' like it!
Moldir yanks Sergeant Buddy Fairchild back by his coat before he can dash into the rain.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Careful, Sergeant. Stay clear of those raindrops.
She scans the horizon. The flood no longer pours out across the land; instead, it ascends back into the sky.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The sea level is dropping.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I can hardly believe it. The plan actually worked.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I guess you're less of a fool than I thought, Mr. Ulrich.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I was only one part of the plan.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I wonder how Vertin's doing down there. She's the one you should be thanking.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I'll make sure I do.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The "Storm" is growing heavy.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I wonder have my people in São Paulo found shelter?

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: I knew I wasn't mad for bringing a few extra Equilibrium Umbrellas. Boss, get under here!
Ulrich nods and looks at the collapsed mountain.
Every trace has been erased by the "Storm." The ferrofluid flows through his tank without any trace of emotion.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The ritual has been disrupted, and the "Flood" is turning into a "Storm."

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Then, does that mean ...

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: All the "Storms" were the result of a failed "Flood"?
Antarctic Sea
On distant ships, Equilibrium Umbrellas snap open one by one.
Admiral Somme looks out over Antarctica.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: The ritual has been halted, just as it was in 1999.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: And now comes another "Storm." History has a way of repeating itself, it seems.
Behind him, crisp boots step forward.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Where will it take us this time? Back to the past? Or into the future?

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Perhaps this is the best outcome we could have hoped for.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: We might have suffered many more casualties.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Agreed, sir.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: The Timekeeper has certainly exceeded her reputation—quite remarkable indeed.

items.speaker: Admiral Somme
items.text: Regardless, the battle is over.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: But our respite will be brief.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: After all, the "Storm" won't last for long.
In the "Storm," firearms and artillery rise one after another.
City Ruins

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Urhm ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto? Nautika?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You're awake! We were searching and searching, and we couldn't find you anywhere, and we were so worried and ... and ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We found you in the sanctuary ruins after the "Flood" subsided. I don't see any issues with your physical condition, but ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: How are you feeling? Any discomfort?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Spinning Wheel ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The only piece of it we found was the one that you were holding in your hand when we found you.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It looks almost identical to the one we have in the suitcase. I assumed it was important, so I put it in the suitcase for safekeeping.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Probably best to keep it in there for now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait. Is that rain I hear?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes. It's the "Storm." The "Flood" transformed into it.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But don't worry. We're safe within the sanctuary walls.
Pushing upright, she looks out.
The "Storm" purges all things.
Yet at the edge of vision, a familiar silhouette appears like a haze within the rising rain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores?
Her feet move on their own, chasing the distant image.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores, wait!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I-I still have things I need to ask you!
The figure stops. This time, she turns.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Vertin.
The "Storm" blurs her face.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: We all walk our own paths, seeking our own answers.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: But our paths will surely cross again.
The rain dissolves the figure, carrying it away—impossible to tell whether anything truly stood there or if it was just a waking dream.
Except for the song, familiar and bright drifting down from beyond the sky.
Sail, sail free, my heart and light.
Wave your home a last goodbye.
Go and seek the Golden Fleece.
In the land of endless peace.
Sail, sail free, my heart and light.
Find your home beneath your feet.
Winter, spring, the years they turn.
Let your heart grow brave and strong.
THE END
